items.passage: Wet clay slapped against the wheel, and the kiln ticked as it cooled, giving off a smell like scorched bread. Gopal had rented the corner bench of the Krakow studio for the winter, and I had come with him only to carry his boxes. Donal arrived at noon with his maps rolled under his arm, a surveyor sent from the city to settle a boundary. He asked Gopal what the field beyond the river was called. "My grandfather called it the Lantern," Gopal said, "but nobody has said that word in forty years." Donal wrote something else on his chart, the number the office preferred. I watched Gopal press his thumb into a bowl he was shaping, leaving a mark he did not smooth away. Later I found myself saying the old name aloud to the empty studio, testing how it sounded, and I was surprised at how much I did not want it to disappear. Outside, a cart rattled over the cobbles toward the market square.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the old name of the field?
options: Amused indifference, since the narrator treats the name as a quaint family joke
Open hostility toward Donal for recording an official number instead
Quiet attachment that the narrator did not expect to feel
Firm confidence that the name will soon be restored on the maps
items.explanation: 서술자는 처음에 짐만 나르러 왔다고 밝혀 이 문제와 거리를 두는 듯 보인다. 그러나 뒤에서 빈 작업실에 옛 이름을 소리 내어 말해 보고, 그것이 사라지지 않기를 바라는 마음에 스스로 놀란다. 두 단서를 연결하면 예상치 못한 조용한 애착이 드러나므로 C가 정답이다. B는 Donal에 대한 적대감이 지문에 없고, D는 이름 복원에 대한 확신이 근거가 없다. A는 이름을 농담처럼 여긴다는 단서가 없다.

items.passage:
Years later, I still climbed to the tank on the roof,
the one we called our ship above Valparaiso,
where Esperanza and I once dropped pebbles in
to hear the dark water answer.

At the funeral she came back without a word of where,
her coat too thin for July, her hands too still.
Rosalinda, she said, as if my name
were something she had borrowed and returned.

I did not ask. I passed her the bread,
I pointed to the chair beside my mother.
Later, on the roof, I lifted the rusted lid
and found the water lower than I remembered,

but still there, still holding the sky.
I dropped one pebble for each year she was gone
and waited, counting, for each small reply.
Below, the harbor cranes swung slowly through the fog.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Esperanza's return?
options: Resentful, because Esperanza refuses to explain where she has been
Indifferent, since the speaker cares more about the old water tank
Anxious, as the speaker fears Esperanza will leave again before night
Accepting, with a patient wish to reconnect despite the silence
items.explanation: 화자는 사촌이 어디 있었는지 묻지 않고 빵을 건네며 자리를 안내해 그녀를 받아들인다. 이후 옥상에서 떠나 있던 해마다 조약돌을 하나씩 떨어뜨리며 대답을 기다리는 모습은 관계를 다시 잇고 싶은 인내심을 보여준다. 두 장면을 연결하면 D가 정답이다. A는 설명이 없다는 점을 활용했지만 화자에게서 원망은 드러나지 않는다. B와 C는 지문에 근거가 약하다.

items.passage: Rain hissed along the window of the train out of Busan, and the compartment smelled of oranges and wet wool. I had taken the trip with Okja, the seamstress who taught me to sew, because she wanted to see the sea once more before closing her shop. Winston, her only apprentice besides me, sat across from us threading a needle he did not need. All morning we talked about next season's patterns as if there would be one. When Okja's hand shook and she dropped her thimble, Winston caught it and handed it back without comment, and I admired him for that small mercy. Yet I felt, too, that our cheerful plans had become a kind of costume we were all wearing. I wanted someone to say the shop was ending, and I knew it would not be me. A vendor rolled a cart past the door, calling out boiled eggs.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the conversation in the compartment?
options: Uneasy about the pretense, though sympathetic to why everyone keeps it up
Grateful that the talk of patterns lets Okja forget her worries entirely
Irritated with Winston for refusing to admit that the shop will close
Hopeful that next season's patterns will persuade Okja to stay open
items.explanation: 서술자는 Winston의 작은 배려를 높이 평가해 모두가 위로하려는 마음을 이해한다. 동시에 밝은 계획이 모두가 입은 의상 같다고 느끼고 누군가 끝을 말해 주기를 바란다. 두 단서를 합치면 가식에 대한 불편함과 공감이 함께 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. C는 Winston을 오히려 높이 평가하는 지문과 맞지 않고, B는 걱정을 완전히 잊는다는 근거가 없다. D는 가게가 계속될 것이라는 희망이 지문에 없다.

items.passage: I was eleven the evening I missed the penalty in front of half of Gdansk, or so it felt, the ball sailing over the crossbar into the dusk. My grandmother Irena had watched from the bench by the fence in her good coat. Walking home, she said nothing about the match. Instead she told me about the year she forgot her lines in a school play and stood frozen while Pavel, her brother, laughed from the third row. "He laughed for a week," she said, "and then he forgot, and so did I." At the time I thought she was only changing the subject. Years later I understood that she had chosen her own embarrassment to stand beside mine, and I still marvel at how carefully she did it. The streetlights along the shipyard road came on one after another.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's adult attitude toward his grandmother's story?
options: Lingering confusion about why she avoided discussing the penalty
Admiring appreciation for the thoughtful way she offered comfort
Mild embarrassment that she shared such a private memory with him
Regret that he did not listen more closely to her advice that night
items.explanation: 어린 시절 서술자는 할머니가 단지 화제를 돌린다고 생각했다. 그러나 훗날 할머니가 자신의 창피한 기억을 일부러 꺼내 손자의 곁에 세워 주었다는 것을 깨닫고 그 세심함에 감탄한다고 말한다. 두 시점을 연결하면 B가 정답이다. A는 어린 시절의 오해를 성인의 태도로 착각한 선택지이고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: "Ninety-eight, Kak Xinyi, he got ninety-eight!" That is what Siti shouted across the night bus in Surabaya, waking half the passengers, and I am writing to you, Mother, because I cannot stop thinking about it. Siti has tutored our brother since spring, and this score is her triumph as much as his. I was proud, truly. But on the ride home she began listing new schools, new fees, a scholarship exam in the capital. Our brother sat between us, holding the paper as if it might tear. I kept nodding, because she had earned her joy, while a cold arithmetic ran in my head about rent and train fares. I am glad of his success, and I am frightened of what it will ask of us. Please tell Father the mango tree by the gate has finally flowered.
items.question: Which choice best describes the letter writer's attitude toward her brother's test result?
options: Pure delight, since the score proves Siti's teaching was worthwhile
Resentment that Siti takes credit for what the brother achieved alone
Pride mixed with worry about the demands the success will bring
Indifference to the score compared with concerns about the household
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 진심으로 자랑스러웠다고 말하면서도 Siti가 새 학교와 학비를 나열할 때 머릿속으로 월세와 기차표를 계산한다. 이후 동생의 성공이 기쁘면서도 그것이 요구할 것들이 두렵다고 밝혀 자부심과 걱정이 공존함을 보여준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 걱정을 빠뜨렸고, B는 Siti가 기쁨을 누릴 자격이 있다는 글쓴이의 말과 맞지 않는다. D는 자부심을 무시한 선택지다.

items.passage: Ottilie owned the diner. Every Tuesday the mayor, Friedrich, came in for coffee and praised the town doctor, who had driven through a snowstorm in January to deliver twins on a farm. Friedrich told the story to anyone at the counter, and each time the twins grew healthier and the snow grew deeper. Ottilie refilled his cup and said nothing. She knew the doctor had not been paid for that night or for most nights since the clinic's budget was cut. When the council met, Friedrich voted against new funding, explaining that the doctor's devotion was the town's pride. Ottilie wrote the vote on a napkin and pinned it beside the menu. Outside, a truck idled by the pumps, its headlights catching the frost on the window.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the snowstorm in which the doctor delivered twins on a farm
To show Ottilie's skill at running a busy roadside diner in winter
To suggest that people should always repay the kindness of others
To expose the gap between praising the doctor and actually paying her
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 시장은 의사의 헌신을 계속 칭찬하지만, 뒷부분에서는 그 헌신을 이유로 예산 증액에 반대표를 던진다. 두 장면의 대비를 통해 칭찬과 실제 지원 사이의 괴리를 드러내는 것이 지문의 목적이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르다. C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Years later, Saoirse would remember the dock more clearly than the war. Her brother Maeve, named for a grandmother and teased for it since boyhood, came back to the lake outside Glasgow in late autumn and sat with her on the wet planks. Their youngest brother was asleep in the cottage. "He'll ask what it was like," Saoirse said. Maeve skipped a stone and watched it sink on the fourth bounce. At supper the boy did ask, and Maeve described the ship's galley, a cat that slept on the anchor chain, a sergeant who sang off-key. Saoirse noticed he left out everything else and that his hands stayed under the table. She did not correct him. In the morning frost lay on the boat's upturned hull, white as flour.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the passage?
options: To show a soldier choosing to shield a young sibling from hard truths
To record the details of daily life aboard a ship during wartime
To argue that children should always be told the full truth about war
To describe the lake near Glasgow as it appeared in late autumn
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Saoirse는 어린 동생이 전쟁에 대해 물을 것이라 걱정하고, 뒷부분에서 Maeve는 고양이와 노래 같은 가벼운 일만 이야기하며 나머지는 빼놓는다. 두 장면을 연결하면 돌아온 병사가 어린 동생을 가장 힘든 진실로부터 보호하는 선택을 보여주는 것이 목적이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화의 세부만 요약했고, D는 배경 묘사에 그친다. C는 지문에 없는 일반적 주장이다.

items.passage:
Nobody wins at breakfast.

A camp dining hall in Kerala. Long tables, steam from rice pots. KAMALA and VIKRAM, rival bakers hired for the summer, stand over a hand-drawn map spread between the jam jars.

KAMALA: Your route to the spice market adds an hour.

VIKRAM: Your route crosses the river where the bridge is out.

KAMALA: (tapping the map) Then we each walk alone, as usual.

(A pause. VIKRAM traces a third line with his finger, half his road and half hers.)

VIKRAM: Or this way. Longer than yours, shorter than mine.

KAMALA: (studying it) You marked the tea stall I like.

VIKRAM: I noticed you stop there.

(KAMALA folds the map carefully and puts it in her apron pocket. Outside, a bell rings for the campers, and a crow lands on the windowsill.)
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that rival workers should always divide their tasks equally
To show two rivals beginning to soften by agreeing on a shared path
To list the practical dangers of traveling to a market in Kerala
To describe how the bakers prepare breakfast for the summer campers
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 제빵사는 서로의 경로를 비판하며 늘 그렇듯 따로 가자고 말한다. 뒷부분에서 Vikram이 두 길을 반씩 섞은 세 번째 길을 그리고 Kamala가 좋아하는 찻집까지 표시했다는 점, Kamala가 지도를 소중히 접어 넣는 모습이 이어진다. 이 대비는 경쟁자들이 공유된 길에 합의하며 누그러지는 과정을 보여주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이고, C와 D는 소재만 빌린 다른 목적이다.

items.passage: Kyoto taught me about stairwells. Ours was narrow and smelled of rain and someone's miso, and it was there that Rajendra handed back the metronome I had given him for his birthday. He said it was too generous, but I heard what he meant: our duo was finished, and he did not want to owe me anything. For a week I resented him. Then I remembered how, during our first winter, he had copied out every page of my score by hand when my bag was stolen, and never mentioned it again. Emilio, our landlord, told me later that Rajendra had stood on the landing a long time before knocking. I began to see the returned gift as his clumsy way of leaving cleanly. Pigeons still nest above the third-floor window.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To recount the details of a birthday gift and how it was returned
To criticize Rajendra for refusing a present from a fellow musician
To trace the narrator's shift from resentment toward understanding
To claim that all musical partnerships eventually come to an end
items.explanation: 서술자는 처음에 선물을 돌려받고 일주일 동안 원망한다. 그러나 Rajendra가 과거에 악보를 손으로 베껴 준 일과 계단참에서 오래 망설였다는 이야기를 떠올리며 그 행동을 깔끔하게 떠나려는 서툰 방식으로 이해하게 된다. 두 근거를 연결하면 원망에서 이해로의 변화를 보여주는 C가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 초기 감정만 반영한다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 주장이다.

items.passage: By the last week of March, the terrace above our house in Shanghai was all mud and seedlings, and my mother still insisted on watering them. I had sold my apartment so I could care for her, though we both knew she was preparing to leave this world, not this hillside. Each morning she pointed to rows I could not tell apart and named them: chives, mustard greens, the beans my father Jianguo had liked. I wrote the names on sticks so I would not forget. Weeks later, when she could no longer climb the steps, she asked only whether the beans had come up. I told her they had, and for once it was true. Now a neighbor's radio drifts over the wall each evening, playing old opera.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain why the narrator decided to sell her apartment in the city
To give practical advice on planting vegetables on a hillside terrace
To suggest that every family should keep a garden for hard times
To show how tending the garden became a way of holding on to her mother
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 서술자는 어머니가 이름을 부르는 작물을 잊지 않으려고 막대에 이름을 적는다. 뒷부분에서 어머니가 콩이 올라왔는지만 묻고 서술자가 사실대로 답하는 장면이 이어진다. 두 장면을 연결하면 정원을 가꾸는 일이 어머니를 붙잡는 방식이 되었음을 보여주는 것이 목적이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 일화의 한 부분만 다루고, B는 소재만 빌린 다른 목적이며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: I am writing to you, Dario, from the back row of the language school in Marseille, where I teach evenings now that the garden no longer needs me. When you bought the house, you kept me on and lent me money for my daughter's surgery, asking only that I repay you when I could. I have enclosed the first part. You will notice it is small. I have also enclosed the planting chart for the lemon trees, with the dates I used to prune them, because you once admitted you did not know where to begin. Please do not think of the chart as interest. I mean it as proof that I have not forgotten what I owe, in money and in the months you gave me. My students, Noemie among them, are arriving with their notebooks.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the letter?
options: To acknowledge a debt of money and time and begin repaying it
To complain that teaching evening classes pays less than gardening
To explain in detail how to prune lemon trees through the seasons
To argue that employers should always lend money to their workers
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 글쓴이는 수술비를 빌려준 Dario에게 첫 상환금을 동봉했다고 말한다. 뒷부분에서는 레몬나무 재배표를 함께 보내며 돈뿐 아니라 내어준 시간에 대한 빚도 잊지 않았다는 증거로 삼는다. 두 부분을 연결하면 돈과 시간의 빚을 인정하고 갚기 시작하는 것이 목적이므로 A가 정답이다. C는 소재만 빌린 다른 목적이고, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이며, B는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Marisol had cooked in her aunt Lucia's kitchen above the bookbinder's workshop for two years before she found the ledger. Inside its cover, in faded ink, was a name: Inés. Lucia snatched it away and said the name belonged to no one now. That evening Marisol noticed that her aunt set out an extra spoon at supper, then quietly put it back. The next week, binding scraps for the shop, Marisol saw the same name stamped into an old leather cover, beside a date from the year her aunt's sister had left Galicia. On Sunday she baked the almond cake her aunt never ordered from the market but always lingered over, and she wrote Inés in sugar on the top. Afterward she swept flour from the floor while the presses thumped below.
items.question: Why does Marisol most likely write the name on the cake?
options: She wants to punish her aunt for hiding the ledger from her
She hopes the cake will win her a promotion in the bookbinder's shop
She senses that her aunt still grieves for the person named
She was asked by a customer at the market to decorate the cake that way
items.explanation: Lucia는 그 이름이 이제 아무의 것도 아니라고 말하지만 저녁 식사에 숟가락을 하나 더 놓았다가 거둔다. 또한 Marisol은 이름 옆의 날짜가 이모의 자매가 떠난 해임을 알게 된다. 두 단서를 이어 읽으면 Marisol이 이모가 여전히 그 사람을 그리워한다고 느꼈기 때문에 이름을 썼음을 알 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, B는 지문에 없는 결과를 동기로 삼았으며, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Solder smoke hung in the radio repair shop in Dakar, sharp as burnt pepper, and the shelves hummed with half-mended sets. Abena, the ferryman's daughter, had promised Kwame that if he waited, she would fix the radio his father had carried across the river every season for thirty years. She worked through the afternoon. When the radio crackled to life, Kwame thanked her and paid, but he did not smile. Earlier he had mentioned that his father no longer remembered the songs. Abena, wrapping the radio in newspaper, asked whether he would like her to leave the old station marked on the dial. He said yes, quickly. She painted a small red line beside the number. A boy outside was selling roasted peanuts from a tin.
items.question: Why does Abena most likely offer to mark the old station on the dial?
options: She wants Kwame to return to her shop for future repairs
She is proud of her work and wants to sign the radio
She was instructed by her father to mark every radio she fixes
She sees that the repair alone cannot restore Kwame's loss
items.explanation: Kwame는 라디오가 고쳐졌는데도 웃지 않고, 앞서 아버지가 더 이상 노래를 기억하지 못한다고 말했다. 두 단서를 이어 읽으면 Abena가 수리만으로는 Kwame가 잃은 것을 되돌릴 수 없음을 깨닫고 옛 방송국을 표시해 주겠다고 제안한 것이므로 D가 정답이다. B는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, A는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각했으며, C는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Once, when I was fifteen, I spent a summer on a tea plantation on Jeju Island, sanding drying racks for Chulsoo, a master carpenter who spoke almost no English. Hemi, another apprentice, translated for us. One afternoon Chulsoo examined my rack and said something short. Hemi told me it meant the joints were weak. I nearly quit. Later I learned the word Chulsoo had used also means not finished yet, a phrase he applied even to his own work. That evening I noticed Hemi resanding my joints alone after the others had left, his translation weighing on him. The next morning he asked Chulsoo to repeat the comment in front of me and translated it again, slowly, with both meanings. Rain had darkened the rows of tea by then.
items.question: Why does Hemi most likely ask Chulsoo to repeat the comment?
options: He wants to correct the harsher meaning his first translation gave
He hopes to impress Chulsoo with his improving language skills
He believes the narrator will leave unless Chulsoo apologizes
He was told by the plantation owner to translate more carefully
items.explanation: Chulsoo가 쓴 단어에 '아직 끝나지 않았다'는 뜻도 있다는 사실과, Hemi가 자신의 번역을 마음에 걸려 하며 홀로 서술자의 이음새를 다시 사포질하는 장면이 단서다. 두 단서를 이어 읽으면 Hemi가 첫 번역이 준 가혹한 의미를 바로잡으려 한 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, C는 결과를 동기로 착각했으며, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: By the third winter of lessons, I had learned to read Etienne's silences better than his words. He taught violin in a spare room of the weaving cooperative in Ohio, where the looms clattered through the wall. After my recital he said only that my bow arm was still lazy. Yet I had seen him in the back row, mouthing the phrasing of the slow movement along with me. Konrad, who ran the cooperative, told me Etienne had asked twice whether anyone had recorded it. The following week Etienne gave me a harder concerto than I was ready for and left before I could protest. I practiced it until my fingers ached. Snow piled against the cooperative's loading door that February.
items.question: Why does Etienne most likely give the narrator a harder concerto?
options: He is dissatisfied and wants to show how weak the recital was
He is quietly proud and thinks the narrator can go further
He hopes the narrator will quit and free his teaching time
He was asked by Konrad to prepare a student for a competition
items.explanation: Etienne은 겉으로는 활 쓰는 팔이 게으르다고만 말하지만, 연주 중 뒷줄에서 악구를 따라 입을 움직이고 녹음이 있는지 두 번이나 물었다. 두 단서를 이어 읽으면 그가 자랑스러움을 숨긴 채 서술자가 더 성장할 수 있다고 믿어 어려운 곡을 준 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 겉으로 드러난 말만 믿은 선택지이고, C는 근거가 없는 동기이며, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Three rules for the metro platform in Cape Town, Sipho had told the delivery boy: stand behind the yellow line, never run for a closing door, and never leave a job half done. Mandla had laughed at the last one. Now they waited for the late train with the widow's half-built birdhouse wrapped in plastic between them. Sipho's wife had started it before she died, and she had asked that it be finished before the rains. Mandla kept checking the departure board and grinning about the paint he had found, the exact green she had wanted. Sipho let himself enjoy the boy's eagerness. Still, he kept touching the plastic, feeling the gap where the roof should be, and wondering whether finishing it would mean letting her go. A pigeon walked the edge of the platform.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the passage?
options: Purely joyful, as both characters celebrate finding the right paint
Mostly anxious, with only a trace of hope about the birdhouse
Hopeful anticipation tinged with a quieter undercurrent of grief
Tense and suspicious, as Sipho doubts Mandla's intentions
items.explanation: 지문에는 Mandla가 원하던 초록 페인트를 찾아 들뜬 모습과 Sipho가 그 열의를 즐기는 기대감이 두드러진다. 그러나 Sipho가 지붕이 빠진 자리를 만지며 완성이 아내를 보내는 것일까 고민하는 모습에서 슬픔이 은은히 깔린다. 따라서 기대감에 슬픔이 섞인 C가 정답이다. A는 슬픔을 빠뜨렸고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Paper cups stacked in a careful tower on the low table between them, one for each hour of the delay in the Bergen hospital waiting room. Anneke had started the tower; Marit had added the fourth cup and steadied the base. They were strangers, both waiting on test results, and somewhere in the second hour they had begun arguing, gently, about whose idea it had been. Anneke said she had built the foundation. Marit pointed out that foundations fall without a top. They laughed, and a nurse glanced over and smiled. Between the jokes, though, Anneke kept looking at the clock, and Marit's foot tapped whenever a door opened. Neither of them asked what the other was waiting to hear. Rain streaked the tall windows overlooking the car park.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the passage?
options: Grim and fearful, with no relief from the long wait
Openly competitive, as the strangers fight over credit
Peaceful and carefree, since the waiting room feels calm
Lighthearted companionship shadowed by unspoken worry
items.explanation: 두 낯선 사람은 컵 탑을 누구 아이디어로 볼지 장난스럽게 다투며 웃고, 간호사도 미소 짓는다. 그러나 Anneke가 계속 시계를 보고 Marit이 문이 열릴 때마다 발을 구르는 모습에서 말하지 않은 걱정이 드러난다. 가벼운 유대가 두드러지고 걱정이 그림자처럼 깔리므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 걱정을 빠뜨렸으며, B는 장난스러운 다툼을 과장했다.

items.passage:
Some apologies arrive late.
Jomo brought his to the courtyard in Addis Ababa
where the fountain had been dry since spring,
and stood beside its cracked stone lip
like a man waiting for water.

Themba did not look up from his book.
Yesterday the new teacher had called him careless
in front of everyone; today he offered
three soft sentences and a borrowed pen.

Themba took the pen. He did not say thank you.
Still, he moved his bag from the bench
so that there was room, a narrow room,
for someone to sit if someone wanted.

Jomo sat. Neither of them spoke.
A sparrow tried the empty basin,
found only dust, and stayed anyway,
turning its head toward the noon bells.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the poem?
options: Guarded reluctance easing slowly into a fragile truce
Tentative warmth that fully dissolves the student's hurt
Bitter hostility that leaves no room for reconciliation
Playful teasing between a teacher and his favorite student
items.explanation: Themba는 고개를 들지 않고 고맙다는 말도 하지 않아 경계심이 두드러진다. 그러나 가방을 치워 좁은 자리를 내주고 Jomo가 앉는 장면에서 조심스러운 화해가 시작된다. 경계가 천천히 누그러지는 연약한 휴전의 분위기이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 상처가 완전히 풀렸다고 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 화해의 단서를 무시했으며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Years later I still think of the monastery guesthouse in Karachi, where Fausto and his twin divided their late father's house on paper over cups of cardamom tea. I was there as Mehreen's friend; she was the child they had once promised the upstairs room, the one with the blue shutters. The brothers were polite, even cheerful, trading jokes about who had snored worse as boys. But each time the upstairs room came up, the jokes stopped and someone refilled the cups too carefully. Mehreen, grown now, said she did not need the room. Fausto said a promise was a promise, and his brother looked out the window. The bell for evening prayer rang across the courtyard, and a novice swept the steps.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the passage?
options: Openly hostile, as the brothers argue bitterly over the house
Cordial on the surface but strained beneath by an unresolved promise
Purely nostalgic, focused on the brothers' happy childhood memories
Solemn and religious, centered on the rituals of the monastery
items.explanation: 형제는 어린 시절 코골이 농담을 나누며 정중하고 쾌활하게 보인다. 그러나 위층 방 이야기가 나올 때마다 농담이 멈추고 찻잔을 지나치게 조심스럽게 채우며, 한 사람은 창밖을 바라본다. 겉은 화기애애하지만 아래에 약속을 둘러싼 긴장이 흐르므로 B가 정답이다. A는 긴장을 과장해 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 긴장을 빠뜨렸으며, D는 배경 소재에만 기댄 어조다.

items.passage: Before dawn on my tenth birthday, Roxana, the keeper of the bakery in Samarkand, let me in while the ovens were still warming and the air smelled of sesame and smoke. Waya, a surveyor visiting from abroad who lodged upstairs, had brought her a gift: a set of gleaming steel bread stamps, the wrong pattern entirely for our round loaves. Roxana thanked him warmly and pressed one into the first dough of the day, and the bread came out stamped with a foreign star. Waya beamed. I watched her face and saw her mouth tighten, just once, before she laughed and called it lucky. All morning she sold the starred loaves to puzzled customers, explaining with great patience. I remember the courtyard cats waiting by the back door for crumbs.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the memory?
options: Tense and embarrassed, as Roxana struggles to hide her anger
Purely festive, celebrating the narrator's tenth birthday
Warm and gracious, with a trace of strained politeness
Mysterious, as the foreign star hints at a hidden secret
items.explanation: Roxana는 선물에 따뜻하게 감사하고 별 무늬 빵을 행운이라 부르며 손님들에게 인내심 있게 설명해 따뜻하고 너그러운 분위기가 두드러진다. 그러나 서술자는 그녀의 입이 한 번 굳어지는 것을 보아 억지스러운 예의가 희미하게 섞여 있음을 알려준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 비중을 뒤집었고, B는 생일이라는 소재만 반영했으며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.
